They will wake the children of Lord’s men from the death, whole mankind, fearful to the doom of this old world; they will call to stand up at once from the steady sleep.

Oft I had to bemoan my sorrow
alone at every dawn. There is no one alive
to whom I would dare
 openly tell my heart. I know as a truth…

late 9th century, Old English Martyrology
Sē Antonius ġesēah þǣs Paules sāwle swā hwīte swā snāw stīgan tō heofonum betweoh engla þrēatas; ond tweġen lēon ādulfan his byrġenne on þǣs wēstenes sande; þǣr resteð Paules līchoma mid yfellīċe dūste bewrigen, ac on dōmes dæġe hē ariseð on wuldor.

Antonius saw Paul's soul, as white as snow, ascend to heaven among throngs of angels; and two lions dug his tomb in the sand of the desert. There lies Paul's body, covered by filthy dust, but on Judgement Day he will arise in glory.
y: From the fusion of Proto-West Germanic *dust (“dust”) and *dunst (“dust, mist, vapour”), from Proto-Germanic *dustą (“dust”) and *dunstą (“dust, mist, vapour”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰew- (“vapour, smoke”). Akin to Hindi धुआं (dhuā̃, “smoke”), Middle Dutch dost, donst, duust (Dutch dons, duist), Old High German tunst, dunst (German Dunst), Low German dust, Icelandic dust, Norwegian dust, Danish dyst.
